chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Safwan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, all from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Ihram is not valid except after a prescribed prayer. If you enter Ihram after it, after the greeting (of prayer), and if it is a voluntary prayer, you pray two cycles and enter Ihram after them. So when you turn from your prayer, praise Allah, extol Him, and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

And say: 'O Allah, I ask You to make me among those who answered You, believed in Your promise, and followed Your command, for I am Your servant and in Your hold. I am protected only by what You protect, and I take only what You give.'

And You have mentioned Hajj, so I ask You to establish it for me upon Your Book and the Sunnah of Your Prophet, strengthen me in what I am weak in, and accept my rituals from me with ease and well-being from You, and make me among Your delegates whom You pleased and chose and named and ordained.

O Allah, perfect for me my Hajj and Umrah. O Allah, I intend Tamattu' with Umrah to Hajj upon Your Book and the Sunnah of Your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). If something occurs that prevents me, then release me where you prevented me, according to the decree You decreed upon me.

O Allah, if it is not a Hajj, then an Umrah. I enter Ihram for You with my hair, skin, flesh, blood, bones, marrow, and nerves, abstaining from women, clothes, and perfume, seeking Your Face and the Hereafter by that.

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And it suffices you to say this once when you enter Ihram. Then stand and walk comfortably. When the ground is level with you, whether walking or riding, then say the Talbiyah.'

key_terms.التَّمَتُّعَ: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the proper supplication and procedure for entering Ihram according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the Sunnah of performing Ihram immediately following a prescribed or voluntary prayer, emphasizing the spiritual transition through a specific supplication that acknowledges divine decree and human dependence. The text highlights the flexibility of the ritual, allowing for a single recitation of the supplication before walking to the state of readiness for the Talbiyah, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the Ahl al-Bayt. It underscores the concept of 'Ihram' not merely as a physical state but as a conscious commitment to God's command, rooted in the Prophet's tradition.
